title: Early recommendations shaped what AI groups chose later
summary: In a controlled music recommendation study, 13 language-model populations evaluated the same 48 unfamiliar song lyrics. When popularity strongly influenced what agents saw, the first 30 agents’ choices predicted later popularity better than recommendations made without popularity information for all 13 populations.
ai_technology: Thirteen language-model populations; Suno v4.5 stimuli

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 §§2–3, Figure 1 design, Figure 5 temporal comparison, appendix robustness and Table S2

evidence.tested: Each model had an independent baseline and eight simulated populations per influence condition. The study compared early choices and independent rankings as predictors of later recommendations.
evidence.unknown: The experiment used synthetic lyrics and a controlled interface, so the magnitude of herding may differ in other recommendation settings.
evidence.ai_role: Thirteen learned language-model populations select and recommend previously unseen Suno-generated lyrics under random exposure to popularity ordering and counts or independent evaluation.
